messages:
samantha: @acme_ops thanks for the report — can you paste the exact 429s you're seeing and whether they're coming from the Redwood gateway or your customer-managed gateway?
acme_ops: seeing 429s at the customer gateway (private VPC). Traffic spikes around 09:30 UTC cause a rush of requests and then everything gets throttled for minutes. Headers include `x-rate-limit-limit: 500`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, then repeated 429s. No 5xx.
aj: Are those Envoy-generated 429s or from a rate-limit-service upstream? Can you share the Envoy access logs (anonymize IPs) and your ingress controller type (nginx-ingress / contour / envoy)?
acme_ops: nginx ingress on k8s (self-managed). We have an Envoy sidecar at the gateway that forwards to Redwood private agent. Logs (redacted):
```
[09:30:12] "POST /v1/generate" 200 1024 "-" x-rate-limit-remaining: 120
[09:30:12] "POST /v1/generate" 200 1024 "-" x-rate-limit-remaining: 119
... spike ...
[09:30:31] "POST /v1/generate" 429 0 "-" x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
[09:30:31] "POST /v1/generate" 429 0 "-" x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
```
acme_ops: our nginx ingress annotations are minimal, using `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "200"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"`. We also have a custom Lua script for burst smoothing.
devon: That Lua burst smoothing can interact poorly with upstream token bucket rules. Two quick questions: are you rate-limiting at both the k8s ingress and the customer gateway (Envoy) simultaneously? And what's the configured burst size on the customer gateway?
acme_ops: ingress + gateway both enforce limits. Gateway uses a leaky-bucket with capacity 500, leak rate 10/sec.
aj: That explains it. When you have a leaky-bucket with small leak rate and ingress that enforces RPS, bursts can pile up and exhaust tokens quickly, causing sustained 429s while the bucket drains. Two options: 1) increase leak/drain rate on the gateway or 2) implement a short token-bucket burst allowance on the ingress so brief spikes don't hit the gateway hard.
samantha: Also check whether the RBAC/auth retries are causing amplified traffic — clients retrying on 401/403 can look like bursts. Any client-side retry policy?
acme_ops: yes, client SDK retries on 500 only. We disabled 429 retries but still see bursts. Some internal jobs do fan-out 50 reqs concurrently at once.

oliver: For a pragmatic repro: create a k8s job that fires 200 concurrent requests to the endpoint in 5s and observe headers. That will mirror your load pattern. Use this curl-based test (replace HOST):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://HOST/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
done
wait
```

Watch `x-rate-limit-remaining` and the gateway logs. If you get a cliff of 429s, it's a capacity/burst-mismatch.
aj: Config tips for nginx ingress: instead of hard `limit-rps`, use a slightly higher `limit-rps` and add `limit-burst: "50"` (annotation differs by controller). For Envoy RLS: set `filter_enabled` and `filter_enforced` with a reasonable `stat_prefix`, and consider a local_cache as a fast short-term smoothing layer.
devon: On the Redwood Private side, our recommended pattern for customer gateways is: - enforce conservative per-connection limits at the k8s ingress to prevent noisy neighbors - allow a small burst window at the gateway level (token-bucket with burst=100-200) - tune KV cache and batching so upstream calls to model serving are rate-limited by request groups rather than raw inbound connections.
acme_ops: if we increase leak rate to 50/sec will that reduce sustained 429s without blowing through tokens/cost?
samantha: yes, but watch downstream: higher leak rate means more tokens consumed quickly, which may raise downstream cost. If cost is a concern, prefer smoothing at the ingress or adding a short client-side jitter/backoff.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline note — changing gateway leak/burst requires gateway restart to pick up new config; plan a brief maintenance window.
aj: Also check `x-forwarded-for` and `remote_addr` normalization. If many clients are NATed behind a few IPs, IP-based rate limiting at ingress can be overly strict. Use a per-api-key or per-token limit instead.
acme_ops: good point — many of those 200 concurrent requests are from 10 worker hosts. We're using IP-based limiting right now. We'll move to token-based headers.

oliver: Follow-up checklist: 1) run the curl repro to confirm cliff, 2) attach ingress config + `kubectl get deploy` for gateway, 3) capture a 60s packet of Envoy access logs and Redwood gateway logs around the spike, 4) test change — increase leak rate to 50 and/or add `limit-burst` to ingress, observe p99 latency and 429s.
devon: If after smoothing you still see frequent 429s, send us: sample request IDs (x-request-id) and a timeline of token counts from the gateway metrics endpoint (/metrics or /debug/rate). We can check if it's token exhaustion vs. misrouted traffic.
samantha: I'll create a short KB entry from this thread with recommended settings for nginx-ingress + Envoy gateway for private VPC customers. It'll include example annotations and a sample Envoy RLS config snippet.
acme_ops: thanks everyone — starting with token-based limits and adding the repro test now. Will update once we have logs. :thumbsup:

ingress-bot: Reminder: nginx-ingress annotation key for burst differs across versions. Use `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps` + controller-specific `limit-burst` or `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-whitespace`? (j/k)
samantha: lol. Keep me posted.
